eyebrow: Ingress needs a controller to do anything

steps.label: Ingress resource
steps.sub: declares host/path routing rules — does nothing alone

steps.label: Ingress controller
steps.sub: ingress-nginx, Traefik, etc. — actually implements the rules

steps.label: Backend Service
steps.sub: an ordinary ClusterIP Service, fronted by the Ingress

code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: shop-routes
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
    - host: api.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /payments
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: payments-api
                port:
                  number: 80
caption: One shared entry point routes /payments to the payments-api Service.

code:
spec:
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - api.example.com
      secretName: api-example-com-tls
  rules:
    - host: api.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: payments-api
                port:
                  number: 80
caption: secretName references a kubernetes.io/tls Secret with the cert and key.

code:
kubectl get ingress shop-routes
kubectl describe ingress shop-routes
caption: describe prints every rule next to the backend Service and port it resolves to.

subtitle: How a Pod finds payments-api by name, not by IP.
